sect2.title: Introduction to DRI
sect2.para: DRI, or Direct Rendering Infrastructure, is a framework that gives direct access to hardware capable of generating graphics for X.org. While Wayland does not use userland DRI, Xwayland that is reponsible for giving X.org application support to Wayland does want the DRI interface. While Xorg-Server and Xwayland want the interface, it doesn't strictly need it if the code for both packages were slightly altered.

Installing the DRI interface is a good idea. DRI comes from Mesa, and there's a couple of ways to install the interface. The interface itself can be downloaded without needing the Mesa tarball. If the tarball is already present, then installing the interface from the tarball can be done instead. The choice is yours.
or (if downloading the files instead of the tarball)

sect2.title: Installation of DRI from the Mesa Tarball
sect2.para: If you have chosen to install DRI from the Mesa tarball, extract the tarball and go into the extracted directory as normal.
After that, install the interface as the &root; user:
Now that the interface has been installed, you need the pkg-config file showing that the interface is present. Create it now as the &root; user:

screen.userinput:
cat > dri.pc << "EOF" prefix=/usr includedir=${prefix}/include
dridriverdir=${prefix}/lib/dri
Name: dri Description: Direct Rendering Infrastructure Version: MESA_VERSION Requires.private: libdrm >= 2.4.109 Cflags: -I${includedir} EOF
sed -i "s/MESA_VERSION/`cat VERSION`/" dri.pc && &install-file; dri.pc -t /usr/lib/pkgconfig/ && rm -vf dri.pc

sect2.title: Downloading DRI from Mesa
sect2.para: If you opted to downloaded the DRI interface from the Internet instead, then there is no setup needed before downloading the interface besides ensuring that you have an Internet connection, installed , and ensured is operational. can be used instead of Wget if you wish.
The files that will be downloaded come directly from the GitLab/FreeDesktop repository for Mesa from a branch or tag that has the same major and minor version of Mesa that's currently in this book.
Now go ahead and download the interface as the &root; user:
Now that the interface has been installed, you need the pkg-config file saying that it's present on the system. Create it now as the &root; user:

screen.userinput:
cat > /usr/lib/pkgconfig/dri.pc << "EOF" prefix=/usr includedir=${prefix}/include
dridriverdir=${prefix}/lib/dri
Name: dri Description: Direct Rendering Infrastructure Version: &mesa-version; Requires.private: libdrm >= 2.4.109 Cflags: -I${includedir} EOF

sect2.para: DRI has now been downloaded and installed.
